summary.headline: Rashi Peripherals Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 51% YoY to INR 4,489 crores, with PAT up 65% to INR 87 crores.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue from operations grew 51% YoY to INR 4,489 crores, EBITDA rose 41% with margin at 2.95%, and PAT grew 65% to INR 87 crores (1.93% margin). For FY26, revenue grew 15% to INR 15,827 crores, EBITDA rose 53% to INR 459 crores (2.90% margin, up 72 bps), and PAT rose 35% to INR 282 crores. Management attributed H2 growth mainly to price increases in the PES category, with H1 growth driven by volume and customer additions. Management guided to a ~20% CAGR and said the PC super cycle could last another 1-2 years, while flagging a possible 5-10% unit decline in CY26 and H2 consumer softness.

financial_highlights.change: Described as healthy vs prior-year outflows

segments.name: PES (Personal computing / enterprise)
segments.commentary: About 58% of business; grew 37% YoY in FY26, aided by higher H2 PC demand and ASPs. Management expects ~20% average price increase in this category going forward.

segments.name: LIT (Lifestyle IT)
segments.commentary: About 42% of business; grew 24% YoY in FY26. Price increases described as routine only; management says LIT is growing about 2x the industry.

segments.name: Semiconductor
segments.commentary: Grew 131% YoY from a small base; customers include large automotive, robotics and IoT manufacturers. Operations moved into a newly created subsidiary; management says meaningful P&L impact is a few years away.

guidance_outlook: Management reiterated a ~20% CAGR (sustained for 20 years) and expects to maintain this trajectory in FY27; regular-business growth aspiration of 15-20% YoY.
Management estimates PES unit market could degrow 5-10% in CY26 (IDC concurs), but with 20-25% price growth, PES revenue could still grow 10-15% on an as-is basis.
Consumer demand could soften in H2 FY27 on affordability; management is discussing 24- and 36-month interest-free EMI schemes with vendors.
Working capital days expected to stay in a similar range in FY27 (CFO).
Distribution PAT margin range of 1.5-1.75% considered applicable to the industry absent mix change; margins described as intact despite price hikes.
Management said the super cycle could continue for another 1-2 years.
Project business (AI data centre) planned for FY27 subject to viability and ROI; funnels of INR 20,000-25,000 crores under consideration.
capex_capacity: Branch network expanded to 55 city branch offices with three new branches added (Nanded, Baramati, Solapur, Maharashtra); 10,000-plus customers across 700-plus towns.
Working capital was increased on inventory to capture demand; management said inventory days cannot fall while regular business grows ~30%.
Project business: FY24-25 included INR 2,000 crores of AI data centre project (Yotta, 512 servers, 4,000 GPUs); no substantial project business in FY26; FY27 plans subject to ROI.
Semiconductor business moved into a separate subsidiary to focus operations and accelerate partnerships and customer acquisition.
Management says it has post-IPO capacity to pick up data centre projects on a selective ROI basis without compromising regular growth.
demand_pricing: Price increases began mainly in H2 FY26; management estimates roughly half of H2 growth (46-47% H2-on-H2) came from pricing, i.e. ~20-22 percentage points.
Management says FY26 growth ex the one large AI project was 31%; FY26 growth without large deals was 15% reported.
Q3 and Q4 FY26 growth reported at 42% and 51% respectively (non-project business).

AI PCs are about 25% of PCs and notebooks sold in India; NVIDIA DGX Spark and Dell (server, storage, PCs, monitors) partnerships cited; Dell described as at low-single-digit share of revenue, expected to reach close to double digits next FY.
IDC: India traditional PC shipments 15.9 million units in CY2025 (+10.2%); IDC flags possible 5-10% dip in CY2026 shipments.
Enterprise refresh delayed by some large corporates during price hikes is reversing as buyers see 30-40% higher prices a year later.
Management said demand is not softening currently; affordability risk in consumer segment in H2.

qa_highlights.question: How much of top-line growth came from pricing vs volume, and what is normalised growth for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Price increases were minimal in H1 and substantial in H2; H2 growth of 46-47% H2-on-H2 included about 20-22 points from price. Management reiterated 20% CAGR for 20 years and expects to maintain it.

qa_highlights.question: What is a PC classified as an AI PC, and how big is that segment?
qa_highlights.answer: Devices with an NPU or high-end processors/GPUs capable of AI workloads; about 25% of PCs and notebooks sold in India are AI PCs, expected to grow further over 1-2 years, lifting ASPs.

qa_highlights.question: Is refresh demand being delayed by price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Some corporates extended refresh cycles initially, but the trend is reversing as buyers realise delay could cost 30-40% more; refresh expected to normalise as in prior years.

qa_highlights.question: Does the semiconductor business carry high working capital, and when will it affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital is higher (100-plus days cited), but gross margins and ROCE are higher than the regular business; the business is small, so meaningful margin impact is a few years away.

qa_highlights.question: How will RP Tech participate in AI data centre projects given capital needs and lower margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Funnels of about INR 20,000-25,000 crores are under consideration; the company will pick projects selectively on ROI without compromising 15-20% regular growth; margins vary by project.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split of revenue from large deals, enterprise and core distribution?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 had no large AI deals (only INR 5-15 crore deals); enterprise non-AI growth is high, driven by NVIDIA solutions; growth ex-Yotta was 31%.

qa_highlights.question: How does the ST Finserv channel finance programme affect working capital and credit risk?
qa_highlights.answer: It is a non-recourse channel finance programme for channel partners; the company bears no credit risk or funding cost unless it draws funds early, which it normally does not.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PAT margin aspiration, and what caused the Q4 gross margin dip?
qa_highlights.answer: Distribution PAT margin range of 1.5-1.75% is typical absent mix change; Q4 gross margin dip was due to additional provisioning for slow-moving inventory, not a structural decline.

risks_watch: Possible 5-10% unit decline in PC market in CY26 and H2 FY27 consumer softness from affordability as prices rise further.
Potential supply shortages in PES due to component (DRAM, NAND, GPU) pricing firmness.
Data centre project participation is capital-intensive with lower margins; scale of funnel conversion uncertain.
Inventory days (56) unlikely to fall while regular business grows ~30%; slow-moving inventory provision taken in Q4.
Semiconductor working capital cycle of 100-plus days; benefits to margin a few years away.
Dependence on Dell ramp-up (low-single-digit share now, expected near double-digit next FY).
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on the PC super cycle and multi-year growth, with growth targets reiterated. Evasive on specifics: declined to give Dell revenue numbers and deferred distribution-channel and margin-trajectory questions offline, and clarified several analyst misreadings of its figures.
key_quotes: So we are very confident to maintain our trajectory of 20% CAGR in the coming year as well.
This is not a 1-quarter tailwind. It is a structural multiyear upgrade super cycle.

Rashi will pick up proportionate to our capacity amongst these opportunities and obviously not run after everything because they are, one, capital intensive, and second, the margins are also lower on this front.

adds.what: Branch network expanded to 55 city branch offices with three new branches (Nanded, Baramati, Solapur, Maharashtra)

growth.why: Management reiterated a ~20% revenue CAGR for FY27, backed mainly by ~20-25% PES price increases and branch expansion, while flagging a possible 5-10% PES unit decline in CY26 and H2 consumer softness; no specific capacity or order numbers were given behind the guidance.
